---
title: "Quickstart"
---

## 1. One name

```bash
icename-gender name "Helga Ingimundardóttir"
```

```
female	dottir
```

Two columns: the estimate, and the [rule](rules.qmd) that decided it. The last name ends in
*-dóttir*, so that settles it.

## 2. What the estimate rests on

```bash
icename-gender name "Helga Ingimundardóttir" --detail
```

```
female	dottir
  Helga                   register  female
  Ingimundardóttir        suffix    female
  agreement: unanimous (female 2, male 0, unisex 0, unknown 0)
```

Each part of the name, and what it says on its own. Here both agree. See
[How certain is it?](certainty.qmd) for when they do not.

## 3. A whole file

Given a CSV with a column of full names:

```{.csv filename="people.csv"}
name
Helga Ingimundardóttir
Ingimundur Helgason
Helga Ingimundarson
```

```bash
icename-gender csv people.csv --column name -o people_gender.csv
```

```{.csv filename="people_gender.csv"}
name,gender,gender_rule
Helga Ingimundardóttir,female,dottir
Ingimundur Helgason,male,given_name
Helga Ingimundarson,female,given_name
```

Every input column is kept; `gender` and `gender_rule` are added. A name no rule decides
gets both empty. A count of the results goes to standard error, so it does not end up in the
output file.

Add `--detail` for the agreement and the female/male evidence counts as well.

## 4. From Python

```python
from icename_gender import classify, explain

classify("Helga Ingimundarson")
# Estimate(gender='female', rule='given_name', given_name='Helga')

explain("Helga Ingimundarson").agreement
# 'conflicting'
```

See the [Python API](python.qmd) for the rest.
